Title: Principal Scientist, Physical AI
Description:
Your New Role and Team

Sanctuary, a world leader in building AI-based control systems for intelligent robots, is seeking a Principal Scientist to support our next generation of robot learning capability. This role sits at the intersection of deep technical understanding and rigorous validation: you will push the boundary of what robots can learn to do, and you will run the experiments that show which approaches have real merit and are worth scaling into a production capability. Deep expertise in at least one or more areas of robot learning — RL and imitation learning, simulation and sim2real, data collection, or world and foundation models — and a working knowledge or awareness of the rest.

This role begins with reviewing everything we are doing and introducing new approaches: you will scope and run focused, high-leverage projects, and bring in support as your work proves out. Successful projects will drive larger projects and more resources.

Our Success Criteria


Identify, scope, and lead research initiatives, working with contributors from across the company
Design and run experiments that validate early hypotheses, surfacing what works, what does not, and what deserves further investment
Demonstrate the merit of new approaches through hands-on experimentation, building the evidence base that demonstrates readiness to scale toward production
Ability to create, develop, and enhance cutting-edge robot learning algorithms — RL, imitation learning, world models, foundation models, or approaches we have not tried — and evaluate their performance in practical robotic applications
Devise training and data collection pipelines to expedite implementation on physical robots
Discover strategies for enhancing current learning processes, considering key performance metrics like sample efficiency, speed, computational resources, and scalability
Collaborate within a diverse team to devise, implement, and harden algorithms for production use, and investigate the root causes in existing implementations
Translate Machine Learning research and trained models into real-world robotic products, working closely with engineering to validate that promising methods hold up as they move toward our cross-platform software framework
Stay current with the latest developments in robot learning — including RL/IL, world models, and foundation models — and their application in robotics


Qualifications

Your Experience


Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or equivalent practical background in robot learning
5+ years of hands-on experience implementing and deploying robotic manipulation tasks, both in simulation and on physical robots
Experience transitioning Machine Learning research and trained models into real-world production
Active involvement integrating Machine Learning models into a robotics platform
Strong technical judgment and the ability to form and defend an independent point of view
Independently able to evaluate a landscape, propose an approach, complete a proof-of-concept and document and articulate the results to a cross-functional team
Comfortable challenging assumptions and driving alignment across technical stakeholders


Deep expertise in at least one of


Applying various Reinforcement Learning and/or Imitation Learning methods, with focus on robotics in the real world
Developing and optimizing large-batch parallel simulations, and proven expertise in sim-to-real transfer
Designing and scaling data collection workflows and datasets for robot learning on physical systems
Building or fine-tuning world models or foundation models for robotics


Nice to Have


Proven expertise in continual learning, employing adaptive model training to improve long-term performance and accuracy
Research contributions at venues such as ICRA, IROS, CoRL, or NeurIPS, or open-source work


Skills


Development with Python 3.8 or later
Working knowledge of PyTorch and/or TensorFlow
Familiarity with ROS2
Strong understanding of modern robot learning methods and their application


Traits


Above all else, a consistently positive attitude and a willingness to do whatever it takes to create robust solutions to complex problems
Pragmatic and outcome-oriented, with a bias toward turning advanced research into real-world products
Entrepreneurial: comfortable scoping and running a project with a cross-functional team
Strong leadership skills in organizing R&D work for projects, with the ability to lead a cross functional team
Curious, adaptable, and willing to go deep into unfamiliar technical areas when needed
Patience, persistence, and attention to detail when resolving performance issues
Ability to multitask and prioritize in a fast-paced environment

Title: Actuarial Specialist
Description:
At Gore Mutual, we’ve always set ourselves apart as a modern mutual that does good. Now, we’re proudly building on that legacy to transform our company—and our industry—for the better.

Effective January 1, 2026, Gore has joined Beneva—the country’s largest mutual insurance company—as part of its Property & Casualty operations in Ontario and Western Canada. During 2026, Gore will combine its operations with Unica Insurance, Beneva’s Ontario-based subsidiary specializing in niche commercial and personal insurance, creating a stronger, more diversified mutual insurer with greater scale and long-term stability.

Every decision and investment remains anchored in long-term benefits to customers, members, and communities. Come join us.

The Actuarial Specialist is responsible for leading the pricing analyses, rating structures and predictive analytics solutions as an independent contributor. The role applies advanced actuarial knowledge to support business decision-making, regulatory requirements, and enhancing pricing methodologies while providing technical guidance and mentorship to less experienced team members. ​​​The Actuarial Specialist reports to the Actuarial Manager and works in conjunction with less experienced analysts. 

What will you do:

Pricing Analysis and Rate Development

Lead complex pricing analyses and investigate trends impacting profitability, growth, retention, and rate adequacy.
Develop and enhance pricing methodologies, rating structures, and actuarial assumptions used in insurance products.
Review pricing results for reasonableness and identify opportunities to improve portfolio performance.
Communicate pricing recommendations and business impacts to management and key stakeholders.

Pricing Models and Portfolio Management

Develop, maintain, and enhance pricing models, including GLMs, machine learning models, and predictive analytics solutions.
Analyze portfolio performance, rate level indications, dislocation impacts, retention, and new business growth.
Conduct scenario testing to quantify the impacts of pricing, underwriting, and market changes.
Recommend enhancements to pricing models, segmentation strategies, and rating algorithms.

Product and Market Analysis

Monitor market trends, competitor pricing, and emerging industry developments.
Support development and implementation of pricing strategies aligned with profitability and growth objectives.
Evaluate new products, coverages, discounts, and underwriting initiatives.
Provide recommendations to improve product competitiveness and customer value propositions.

Model Development and Technical Innovation

Design, build, and maintain actuarial pricing models and automated analytical processes.
Develop solutions using actuarial software, SQL, Python, R, Earnix, or other analytical tools.
Improve efficiency through automation, data visualization, and process optimization.
Evaluate emerging analytical techniques and industry best practices in pricing and predictive modelling.

Regulatory Filings and Pricing Governance

Support rate filings and regulatory approval processes.
Prepare technical documentation, exhibits, and actuarial support for pricing initiatives.
Ensure pricing analyses comply with regulatory requirements, actuarial standards, and internal governance practices.
Contribute to implementation and monitoring of approved rate changes.

Technical Leadership and Professional Development

Act as a subject matter expert for pricing projects and strategic initiatives.
Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and peer review support to analysts and senior analysts.
Assist with training, knowledge sharing, and development of pricing team capabilities.
Continue professional development through CAS/FCIA progression and industry research.

What skills will you need:

Undergraduate degree in Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field, with FCAS/FCIA designation or ACAS nearing Fellowship preferred.
5-8 years of pricing experience within a P&C insurance company.
Strong knowledge of actuarial pricing techniques, predictive modelling, and data analytics.
Experience developing and validating GLMs and other predictive models.
Advanced proficiency with Excel, actuarial software, and pricing platforms such as Earnix.
Strong SQL, Python, R, or equivalent programming skills.
Knowledge of insurance product design, rate indications, regulatory filings, and portfolio management.
Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to translate complex analytical findings into actionable business recommendations.

The expected base salary range for this position is $97,500 - $147,500. Depending on your relevant experience, skills, qualifications, market conditions and business needs, base compensation may vary. You have the potential to earn more through Gore Mutual’s discretionary bonus program which gives you an opportunity to increase your total compensation, provided the business meets its performance targets and you meet your individual goals.

Please note: This range reflects the expected base salary for this role but may not represent the full compensation range for all experience and skill levels. During the recruitment process, we will discuss and consider how your unique qualifications align with the broader range for this position.

Gore Mutual is proud to offer a comprehensive total rewards package which includes extended health and dental benefits, disability insurance, retirement plan matching, paid time off, recognition and perk programs.

 

 

 

This posting pertains to an existing vacancy that is actively being filled.

 

Accessibility for applicants

Gore Mutual Insurance Company is committed to providing accommodations for people with disabilities during all phases of the recruiting process, including the application process.

If you require accommodation because of a disability, we will work with you to meet your needs. Contact us and a human resources representative will consult with you to determine an appropriate accommodation.

Should you request an accommodation during the interview process, please notify your Talent Acquisition Consultant.

Title: Advanced Data Analyst - EA SPORTS™ FC
Description:
Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Advanced Data Analyst, Experimentation Lead - FC Ultimate Team

As one of the largest sports entertainment platforms in the world, EA SPORTS FC is redefining football with genre-leading interactive experiences, connecting a global community of fans to The World's Game through innovation and unrivaled authenticity.

With more opportunity than ever to design, innovate and create new, immersive experiences that bring joy, inclusivity, and connection to fans everywhere, we invite you to join our passionate and dynamic team as we pioneer the future of football fandom.

The FC Data & Analytics team is seeking an Advanced Data Analyst to join our Ultimate Team (UT) function. Reporting to a Senior Manager, you will lead the Experimentation program for FC Premium Analytics. You’ll also collaborate closely with data, production, and product management partners to drive informed decision-making within a dynamic live service environment.

We are looking for a candidate who is excited at the prospect of cultivating and uncovering actionable insights from live player data and contributing to the sustained success of one of the industry's most prominent live service products. In this role, you will act as a data leader, driving design, implementation, and evaluation of numerous player-facing experiments.

What You'll Do On Our Team


Collaborate with production teams to define telemetry requirements, ensuring robust data collection and validity.
Design and implement player-facing experimentation using best practices in a complex, live environment
Write and maintain complex SQL and scripting workflows to extract, transform, and validate large-scale telemetry datasets
Build and maintain scalable dashboards that translate complex datasets into clear, actionable business insights for cross-functional partners
Explore user behavioral patterns through experimentation to identify opportunities for improving player experiences and to inform live content release strategies
Present analytical findings clearly and effectively to stakeholders of all seniority levels to facilitate informed decision-making
Act as a subject-matter expert in all things experimentation, helping to drive adoption of a data-driven, test-and-learn focused culture across FC’s development team


What We're Looking For


Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Operations Research) or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of technical experience in data analytics, with a focus on performing quantitative analysis with large datasets to guide decision-making
Expert knowledge or equivalent practical experience in leading an experimentation function for a live product
Proficiency in SQL with the ability to extract data from complex, multi-source systems.
Hands-on experience with data visualization software (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).
Strong programming skills (e.g., Python, R) with experience writing scripts for data transformation and statistical analysis
Passion for gaming or previous experience in the gaming industry is considered a strong plus.


Pay Transparency - North America

If you reside in a different location, a recruiter will advise on the applicable range and benefits. Pay offered will be determined based on a number of relevant business and candidate factors (e.g. education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, or business needs).

PAY RANGES


British Columbia (depending on location e.g. Vancouver vs. Victoria) *$114,300 - $156,200 CAD


Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at EA.

For Canada, we offer a package of benefits including vacation (3 weeks per year to start), 10 days per year of sick time, paid top-up to EI/QPIP benefits up to 100% of base salary when you welcome a new child (12 weeks for maternity, and 4 weeks for parental/adoption leave), extended health/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, disability insurance, retirement plan to regular full-time employees. Certain roles may also be eligible for bonus and other incentive programs.

We’re proud to have an extensive portfolio of games and experiences, locations around the world, and opportunities across EA. We value adaptability, resilience, creativity, and curiosity. From leadership that brings out your potential, to creating space for learning and experimenting, we empower you to do great work and pursue opportunities for growth.

Title: Principal Resource Geologist
Description:
Location: Vancouver, BC, Canada

Employment Type: Regular Full Time

Workplace Type: Hybrid

About Our Vancouver Office

Located in the heart of downtown Vancouver, between the Pacific Ocean and the Coast Mountains, Teck’s Corporate Office sits in one of Canada’s most culturally diverse cities.

Surrounded by world-renowned nature and globally inspired cuisine, the office brings together many of Teck’s corporate functions - all working toward Teck’s purpose of providing the essential resources the world relies on.

Role Overview

Strategic Planning (SP) at Highland Valley Copper (HVC) is responsible for ensuring the long-term (3+ year) value and resiliency of the operation. The Geology function within SP provides authoritative geological and resource knowledge across all four pits to ensure optimal extraction of value across the full mining value chain.

As Principal Resource Geologist, you are the technical authority and accountable owner of the HVC Mineral Resource Models. You provide oversight, assurance, and governance for resource model development, updates, and application, ensuring models are technically robust, auditable, fit-for-purpose, and consistently applied across Life of Asset (LOA) planning, reserves, mine planning, and strategic decision-making.

This role extends beyond model construction to include coordination and alignment with downstream users of the models—including planning, engineering, operations, metallurgy, and projects—to ensure correct interpretation, appropriate use, and clear communication of uncertainty and risk. You will set standards, define workflows and expectations, and ensure consistency in how resource models inform business decisions at HVC.

You are a recognized technical leader with deep expertise in geostatistics, estimation, and complex porphyry systems, combined with the judgment and influence required to guide high-impact decisions. You are expected to mentor senior practitioners, and influence across disciplines.

This position reports to the Chief Geologist - HVC, SP Geology, and is based in Vancouver, BC, with the option to work remotely up to two days per week. Regular travel to HVC is required (approximately 1 week every 4–6 weeks, with additional travel as business needs dictate).

Key Responsibilities

Safety & Leadership


Act as a courageous and visible safety leader by actively promoting, endorsing, and role-modeling Teck’s safety, environmental, and sustainability values in all interactions and decisions
Take proactive ownership of safety performance by identifying improvement opportunities, engaging stakeholders, and driving actions through to measurable outcomes
Actively participate in safety conversations, field engagements, and risk assessments to reinforce a strong safety culture
Embed safety, hazard awareness, and risk-based thinking into all geological modelling activities, workflows, and decision-support processes


Technical Authority & Governance


Serve as the technical authority for Mineral Resource Models at HVC, accountable for methodology selection, assumptions, validation, and model integrity
Establish, maintain, and evolve standards, guidelines, and best practices for resource modelling, estimation, and classification at HVC
Provide technical sign-off and assurance for resource models used in LOA planning, strategic studies, projects, and public disclosure.


Resource & Reserve Oversight


Provide senior leadership and technical oversight of the annual Resource and Reserve (R&R) process, ensuring compliance with internal standards and external reporting codes
Interface with Qualified Persons, auditors, and reviewers, addressing technical challenges and defending methodologies and outcomes


Cross-Functional Coordination & Model Use


Lead engagement with mine planning, engineering, metallurgy, operations, and projects teams to ensure appropriate and consistent use of resource models
Clearly communicate model assumptions, limitations, uncertainty, and risk to non-geologists to support informed business decisions
Resolve technical misalignment between resource models and downstream applications


Geological Understanding & Model Evolution


Maintain and continuously refine a deep understanding of the HVC mineral system and its spatial, geological, and metallurgical controls
Oversee the integration of geology, structure, geochemistry, geophysics, geometallurgy, and production reconciliation into evolving models
Guide decisions on model resolution, estimation approaches, and classification strategies aligned with business objectives


Innovation & Continuous Improvement


Champion the adoption of advanced and fit-for-purpose modelling approaches, including rapid modelling workflows, conditional simulation, uncertainty analysis, and scenario evaluation
Evaluate advanced modelling and planning techniques leading piloting and implementation where value is demonstrated


Strategic Programs & Advisory Role


Provide senior technical input into the design and prioritization of resource confidence, geometallurgical, geotechnical, and expansion/exploration programs
Act as a trusted advisor to Strategic Planning and site leadership on resource-related risks, opportunities, and trade-offs


Capability Building & Mentorship


Provide technical leadership, mentorship, and coaching to senior and developing geoscientists across HVC and Teck
Build organizational capability by sharing knowledge, reviewing work, and fostering a culture of inclusive technical excellence and rigor.


Qualifications


Degree in Geoscience or a related discipline (e.g., geostatistics, geometallurgy, geochemistry). MSc or PhD strongly preferred;
Registered Professional Geoscientist (or eligible) with Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia
12+ years of progressive experience in resource geology within mining operations, advanced projects, or applied research, including significant experience at a senior level;
Demonstrated accountability for complex resource models supporting LOA planning, reserves, and strategic investment decisions
Expert-level understanding of geostatistics, estimation theory, resource classification, and uncertainty management
Advanced proficiency in 3D geological modelling and estimation software (Leapfrog GEO, EDGE required; Vulcan or equivalent an asset)
Extensive experience with porphyry copper deposits and large, complex open pit operations
Strong background in geochemistry and integrated multi-disciplinary data analysis across the mining value chain
Advanced quantitative and analytical skills, including expert use of R, Python, ioGAS, or similar tools; experience applying data science or machine learning techniques to geological problems is an asset
Proven ability to influence without authority and operate effectively across disciplines and organizational boundariesExceptional written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to convey complex technical concepts to diverse audiences.


Leadership Competencies


Demonstrates visible leadership in health, safety, environment, community, and sustainability
Proven ability to build cross-functional partnerships through collaborative influence and constructive feedback, ensuring stakeholders feel supported
Demonstrates emotional intelligence while challenging the status quo to ensure a culture of mutual respect
Acts with integrity, sound judgment, and accountability, setting the technical and ethical standard for others
Thinks strategically, balancing technical rigor with business value and practicality
Drives results through influence, prioritization, and disciplined execution
Understands and navigates organizational systems, processes, and governance to achieve outcomes.


Pay Range: CAD $138,000 - $170,000 per year

The actual amount offered is determined based on the successful candidate’s relevant experience, skills, and competencies and considers internal equity.

Why Teck

At Teck, your work matters—to the world, to our communities and to your future.

As a leading Canadian resource company, we focus on responsibly providing the metals essential for global development and the energy transition while caring for the people, communities and land that we love. We do this guided by our values that, together, form The Teck Way. At Teck, you’ll find purpose-driven work, a culture of respect and inclusion, and the opportunity to grow your career while helping build a better world.

Apply with us

Take the next step in your career by applying for the Principal Resource Geologist role. We review applications on a rolling basis and encourage you to apply, even if your background doesn’t match every requirement. We value diversity and are committed to an inclusive, barrier-free hiring process. Reasonable accommodations are available upon request.

Experience with predictive modeling or machine learning techniques applied to P&C insurance.

Title: System Optimization Specialist Engineer (FTT)
Description:
Job Location: Edmonds, Burnaby, BC (Lower Mainland)

Employment type: Temporary, Full-time (37.5 hrs/wk), approximately 14 months (until about December 2027)

Flexible Work Role: Hybrid

Annual Salary: $131,100.00 - $165,800.00

Requisition: 52518811

A workplace powered by you

At BC Hydro, we're working towards creating a cleaner and more sustainable future for all British Columbians and need people like you to help us. A career at BC Hydro is meaningful and provides you the opportunity to be part of a talented, inclusive, and diverse team. We offer a healthy work-life balance, competitive wages, a comprehensive benefits package, and training opportunities to support you in your career growth. We're proud to be ranked as one of B.C.'s Top Employers and one of Canada's Best Diversity Employers.

What you'll do

Generation System Operations (GSO) is providing an exciting 14 month rotation opportunity to work with our experienced engineers within the System Optimization group.

BC Hydro operates a 13,200 MW system of hydroelectric, thermal, and market resources. Within Generation System Operations (GSO), energy, capacity, and water planning are managed by teams organized by planning time horizons from real time to five years.

In GSO, the System Optimization (SO) group of ten engineers plans the optimal use of energy and capacity for our major reservoirs and generation assets to meet domestic load and inform Powerex trade flexibility. The SO team holds a unique role, liaising with and informing decisions across multiple BC Hydro business lines: Operations Stations and Transmission, Energy Planning, Project Delivery, Regulatory, Finance, Customer and Corporate Affairs, and our trade subsidiary, Powerex. The SO team reports out, monthly, to VP of Operations and our CFO.

The System Optimization engineers plan our monthly to 5-year energy supply forecasts and our within monthly load resource balance options considering uncertainty associated with our surplus or deficit energy positions. The SO modellers are the touchpoint between Powerex, Finance, and Operations for energy management strategies, the operational balance between our major reservoir systems, Peace and Columbia, and optimization of our consolidated net revenue of operations. Critical to these functions is the SO team's responsibility for supporting and developing new planning tools for system energy optimization and managing data analytics.

System Optimization Responsibilities:

Develop, document, and maintain proprietary models and software used to analyze, optimize, and simulate the physical and economic operation of BC Hydro's integrated generation assets: Hydro with reservoir storage, run of river hydro, wind, and thermal.
Work directly with our wholesale electricity traders (Powerex), with GSO's 24/7 operations team (PSOSE) and Operation Planning Engineers (OPEs), field outage schedulers, Corporate Finance, Regulatory, Energy Planning, Load Forecasting, and Project Delivery to optimize generation, reservoir storage, and outage planning.
Optimize system energy production and storage considering uncertainty in system loads, reservoir inflows, outages, Energy Purchase Agreements, and market prices. Provide direction on setting the marginal values for energy stored in our large hydroelectric reservoirs.
Integrate system planning for BC Hydro's largest generation and storage systems, the Peace and Columbia, including planning operations under the Columbia River Treaty.
Inform and plan to manage energy and capacity deficit and surplus positions under short term time horizons (daily to 6 months) with PSOSE, Powerex, and Stations and Field Operations. Provide scenarios for financial and reliability analysis associated with major outage planning, evolving system issues and policy alternatives. Analyze input data sources and model results for relevancy, reliability, and validity.
Prepare and present monthly reports and advice to the Executive and finance related to system modeling, security of energy supply, financial forecasts, and risk. Communicate and problem solve effectively with BC Hydro VP, Directors, engineers, market traders, finance, software consultants, and other staff, both within BC Hydro and externally, for the purposes of gathering and relaying information and resolving new issues of concern.

What you bring

Engineering degree recognized by Canadian Universities and registered, or eligible for immediate registration, as a Professional Engineer with EGBC.
Applicant may be hired as a Senior Engineer (8+ years) or Specialist Engineer (10+ years) depending on level of experience in the following areas: Software development; Economic modeling and analysis; Stochastic programming and/or development of optimization software; Storage based hydroelectric management and modelling; Generation and Transmission outage planning and dispatch; and/or Graduate degree(s) or equivalent experience in Water Resource Management, Applied Mathematics or Economics with specialization in optimization of Energy Systems, Energy Markets, and/or Finance.
Applied programming background in Java and/or R. Experience in data analytics & regression model development and data transformations. Experience in reporting and enterprise data management platforms (Power BI, Fabric, etc.).
Ability to make decisions in tight time frames and under pressure, while working with an extensive array of decision support models. Able to apply creative and critical problem solving to emerging issues. Able to multi-task and set priorities to achieve long term goals.
Engaging interpersonal, oral, and written technical communication and presentation skills.
Ability to provide direct or indirect work leadership to engineers and other technical stakeholders and Project Delivery on water conveyance and generation management.

What we offer

A comprehensive benefits package
A minimum of 15 paid vacation days
A lifetime pension
Flexible work model, depending on your role type
Training and development courses

For more information on the benefits we offer, visit bchydro.com/benefits.

What else you should know

This is a temporary opportunity until approximately December 2027.
Applicants who do not meet full qualifications or those with lesser work experience may be considered for a lower level position.

Please be advised that this role has been assessed as safety sensitive and pre-qualification alcohol and drug testing will be required as a pre-condition to employment.

How to apply

Apply online by October 12, 2026: view and apply for this job on the BC Hydro Careers site.

BC Hydro is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified job seekers. If you're a person with a disability, please let us know by emailing RecruitmentHelp@bchydro.com, as adjustments can be made to help support you in your application process.

Title: Research Data Technologist
Description:
Job Title

Research Data Technologist

Job Category

Non Union Technicians and Research Assistants

Job Profile

Non Union Salaried - Research Assistant /Technician 3

Job Family Group

Staff - Non Union

Department

Keown Laboratory Division of Nephrology | Department of Medicine | Faculty of Medicine

Compensation Range

$4,845.17 - $5,713.66 CAD Monthly

Job End Date

March 31, 2027

Posting End Date

October 23, 2026

Note: Applications will be accepted until 11:59 PM on the Posting End Date.

Please note this is a one (1) year fixed term position. However, there is a possibility of renewal.

At UBC, we believe that attracting and sustaining a diverse workforce is key to the successful pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning for all faculty, staff and students. Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career.

Job Summary

The Research Data Technologist will work as a member of an interdisciplinary team including clinicians, research scientists, statisticians, software developers, and trainees at UBC and collaborating institutions. The incumbent will support research activities by organizing, processing, analysing, and reporting biomedical data under the direction of senior research team members. In addition, they will support the preparation, quality control, analysis, and interpretation of biomedical datasets, including clinical, molecular, genomic, and imaging data. The incumbent will use established analytical methods and software tools and contribute to data organization, visualization, reporting, and other research activities supporting translational research projects. The incumbent will participate in projects involving data processing, visualization, clinical data integration, and selected applications of statistical and computational methods. Work will be performed using established procedures and under the guidance of senior members of the research team.

The Department of Medicine provides excellence in research, teaching, and clinical services related to the nature, cause, and prevention of adult diseases. As the largest Department in the Faculty of Medicine, comprising 18 Divisions and more than 1,200 faculty and staff located throughout British Columbia, the Department is committed to fostering research excellence, supporting learners and faculty, and contributing to the health of the Province of British Columbia.

Organizational Status

The successful candidate will report to the Principal Investigator (Dr. Paul Keown), with day-to-day oversight provided by the Research Associate, Data Manager and/or senior research team members. The Research Data Technologist will work as a member of an interdisciplinary team including clinicians, research scientists, statisticians, and trainees at UBC and collaborating institutions. The Research Data Technologist will receive direction and training appropriate to assigned projects and will provide regular updates on assigned activities and findings, with the day-to-day oversight given by the Research Associate in the Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine

Work Performed


Perform routine data preparation, cleaning, quality checks, and organization for biomedical research datasets.
Use established analytical methods, software tools, and procedures to support research data analysis.
Prepare datasets and analysis outputs for use by researchers, statisticians, and other members of the research team.
Support the processing, quality control, integration, and management of molecular, genomic, clinical, and imaging data.
Develop or modify basic scripts, spreadsheets, and analytical tools to support data processing, visualization, and reporting.
Assist with the application of statistical, machine learning, or other computational methods under the direction of senior team members.
Support data visualization, image analysis, and other analytical activities as required by research projects.
Assist with maintaining research data files, analysis environments, and related computational resources.
Work with researchers and other team members to clarify data requirements and support agreed research activities.
Identify and report data quality issues, workflow problems, or unexpected results to senior research team members.
Assist with testing, documentation, quality assurance, and reproducibility of analyses and data workflows.
Assist with the organization, storage, security, and appropriate handling of research data in accordance with institutional and ethical requirements.
Prepare clear documentation, data summaries, tables, figures, and other research materials.
Assist with established analytical and data management procedures for new and ongoing research projects.
Contribute data summaries, figures, and other materials to scientific reports, presentations, publications, and grant applications.
Maintain familiarity with relevant data analysis tools and procedures and participate in training as required.


Consequence of Error/Judgement

All duties performed by the Research Data Technologist must adhere to data privacy and confidentiality policies, standard operating procedures, and UBC policies. Errors in data handling, analysis, or reporting could affect research results, delay study activities, or compromise data integrity. The Research Data Technologist is expected to follow established procedures and seek guidance from senior research team members when non-routine issues or decisions arise.

Supervision Received

The Research Data Technologist will report to the Principal Investigator (Dr. Paul Keown) with day-to-day oversight provided by the Research Associate. The incumbent may also receive direction from senior research team members and/or senior project co-lead(s), dependent on project. They will also receive necessary training from the Bioinformatician, as well as other members of the research team. The candidate is expected to provide regular research activity updates and present research findings to the team members

Supervision Given

The Research Data Technologist will not have formal supervisory responsibilities. The incumbent may provide basic guidance to students or other team members on routine data procedures when requested.

Minimum Qualifications

Completion of a relevant technical program or a university degree in a relevant discipline and a minimum three years of related experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience.


Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one’s own
Demonstrates a commitment to enhancing one’s own awareness, knowledge, and skills related to equity, diversity, and inclusion


Preferred Qualifications

Education, Training and Experience


Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Bioinformatics, Statistics, Computational Biology, or a related discipline.
Additional training or a Master's degree is considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience in data analysis, research, bioinformatics, statistics, or a related area is preferred.
Experience working with research, healthcare, or scientific datasets is preferred.
Experience in biomedical research, healthcare, genomics, imaging, or related environments is considered an asset.
Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one's own.


Skills And Abilities


Working knowledge of common data analysis and spreadsheet software and/or a programming language such as Python or R.
Ability to clean, organize, and perform basic quality checks on research data.
Ability to use established analytical methods and software tools to support research activities.
Familiarity with data visualization and preparation of tables, figures, and reports.
Familiarity with research databases, data management practices, or biomedical datasets is an asset.
Familiarity with version control or other reproducible research practices is an asset.
Ability to follow established procedures for data privacy, confidentiality, and responsible data stewardship.
Ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical team members.
Demonstrated ability to work independently on assigned tasks and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills.
Ability to manage assigned tasks and meet established deadlines.
Commitment to privacy, confidentiality, and responsible data stewardship.
Ability to manage multiple projects and competing deadlines.
Commitment to privacy, confidentiality, and responsible data stewardship.

In addition, they will support the preparation, quality control, analysis, and interpretation of biomedical datasets, including clinical, molecular, genomic, and imaging data. The incumbent will use established analytical methods and software tools and contribute to data organization, visualization, reporting, and other research activities supporting translational research projects. The incumbent will participate in projects involving data processing, visualization, clinical data integration, and selected applications of statistical and computational methods. Work will be performed using established procedures and under the guidance of senior members of the research team.

The Department of Medicine provides excellence in research, teaching, and clinical services related to the nature, cause, and prevention of adult diseases. As the largest Department in the Faculty of Medicine, comprising 18 Divisions and more than 1,200 faculty and staff located throughout British Columbia, the Department is committed to fostering research excellence, supporting learners and faculty, and contributing to the health of the Province of British Columbia.

Organizational Status

The successful candidate will report to the Principal Investigator (Dr. Paul Keown), with day-to-day oversight provided by the Research Associate, Data Manager and/or senior research team members. The Research Data Technologist will work as a member of an interdisciplinary team including clinicians, research scientists, statisticians, and trainees at UBC and collaborating institutions. The Research Data Technologist will receive direction and training appropriate to assigned projects and will provide regular updates on assigned activities and findings, with the day-to-day oversight given by the Research Associate in the Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine

Work Performed

  • Perform routine data preparation, cleaning, quality checks, and organization for biomedical research datasets.
  • Use established analytical methods, software tools, and procedures to support research data analysis.
  • Prepare datasets and analysis outputs for use by researchers, statisticians, and other members of the research team.
  • Support the processing, quality control, integration, and management of molecular, genomic, clinical, and imaging data.
  • Develop or modify basic scripts, spreadsheets, and analytical tools to support data processing, visualization, and reporting.
  • Assist with the application of statistical, machine learning, or other computational methods under the direction of senior team members.
  • Support data visualization, image analysis, and other analytical activities as required by research projects.
  • Assist with maintaining research data files, analysis environments, and related computational resources.
  • Work with researchers and other team members to clarify data requirements and support agreed research activities.
  • Identify and report data quality issues, workflow problems, or unexpected results to senior research team members.
  • Assist with testing, documentation, quality assurance, and reproducibility of analyses and data workflows.
  • Assist with the organization, storage, security, and appropriate handling of research data in accordance with institutional and ethical requirements.
  • Prepare clear documentation, data summaries, tables, figures, and other research materials.
  • Assist with established analytical and data management procedures for new and ongoing research projects.
  • Contribute data summaries, figures, and other materials to scientific reports, presentations, publications, and grant applications.
  • Maintain familiarity with relevant data analysis tools and procedures and participate in training as required.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

All duties performed by the Research Data Technologist must adhere to data privacy and confidentiality policies, standard operating procedures, and UBC policies. Errors in data handling, analysis, or reporting could affect research results, delay study activities, or compromise data integrity. The Research Data Technologist is expected to follow established procedures and seek guidance from senior research team members when non-routine issues or decisions arise.

Supervision Received

The Research Data Technologist will report to the Principal Investigator (Dr. Paul Keown) with day-to-day oversight provided by the Research Associate. The incumbent may also receive direction from senior research team members and/or senior project co-lead(s), dependent on project. They will also receive necessary training from the Bioinformatician, as well as other members of the research team. The candidate is expected to provide regular research activity updates and present research findings to the team members

Supervision Given

The Research Data Technologist will not have formal supervisory responsibilities. The incumbent may provide basic guidance to students or other team members on routine data procedures when requested.

Minimum Qualifications

Completion of a relevant technical program or a university degree in a relevant discipline and a minimum three years of related experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one’s own
  • Demonstrates a commitment to enhancing one’s own awareness, knowledge, and skills related to equity, diversity, and inclusion

Preferred Qualifications

Education, Training and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Bioinformatics, Statistics, Computational Biology, or a related discipline.
  • Additional training or a Master's degree is considered an asset.
  • Demonstrated experience in data analysis, research, bioinformatics, statistics, or a related area is preferred.
  • Experience working with research, healthcare, or scientific datasets is preferred.
  • Experience in biomedical research, healthcare, genomics, imaging, or related environments is considered an asset.
  • Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one's own.

Skills And Abilities

  • Working knowledge of common data analysis and spreadsheet software and/or a programming language such as Python or R.
  • Ability to clean, organize, and perform basic quality checks on research data.
  • Ability to use established analytical methods and software tools to support research activities.
  • Familiarity with data visualization and preparation of tables, figures, and reports.
  • Familiarity with research databases, data management practices, or biomedical datasets is an asset.
  • Familiarity with version control or other reproducible research practices is an asset.
  • Ability to follow established procedures for data privacy, confidentiality, and responsible data stewardship.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical team members.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently on assigned tasks and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills.
  • Ability to manage assigned tasks and meet established deadlines.
  • Commitment to privacy, confidentiality, and responsible data stewardship.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and competing deadlines.
  • Commitment to privacy, confidentiality, and responsible data stewardship.

Title: Data Analyst - Portfolio Reporting, Real Estate Debt
Description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description:

The Data Analyst - Portfolio Reporting, Real Estate Debt (12 month Contract) will report directly to the Director, Portfolio Reporting, Real Estate Debt. We are seeking a highly motivated individual with a background in Data Science or Data Analytics who is looking to develop their career in an entrepreneurial and high-energy environment. Embedded within the business, this role supports management reporting, forecasting, and portfolio analysis across the RE Debt portfolio, in addition to being the primary liaison to ED&A and IT — translating reporting requirements into data specifications and building data flows from the Enterprise Data Platform through to the reporting layer. This position also works closely with the Real Estate Debt Investment, Accounting, and Operations teams, FP&A, and Portfolio Management teams across QuadReal.

Role Description:


Support scenario modelling, cash flow forecasting, leverage and liquidity analysis through Anaplan, supplemented by ad-hoc financial models as needed, using AI-assisted development for efficiency and quality control
Analyze portfolio exposures, return attribution, and market trends, and support the development of presentation materials with AIenhanced insights and visualization
Assist in the preparation of monthly, quarterly and ad hoc management reports for senior management, Board of Directors and BCI
Support real estate debt investment underwriting by providing portfolio impact analysis
Assist with ad hoc research projects for benchmarking, peer analysis, risk analysis, and other relevant topics
Query and extract data from enterprise data platforms to support portfolio reporting and analytics needs
Develop and maintain business logic, portfolio calculations, and data transformation rules that underpin reporting outputs
Serve as the primary business-side liaison to IT and ED&A, translating reporting requirements into data specifications and validating platform outputs
Support data enablement initiatives and ongoing data management and governance priorities across the RE Debt portfolio
Validate and reconcile data collected from different systems using AI-powered anomaly detection to improve data quality and identify process improvement opportunities


Experience And Qualifications:


University degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g. Statistics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field) OR a background in Economics, Finance or a related business field. CFA or similar designation is a plus
2–3 years of experience working in a data analyst role, ideally in investment management or real estate.
Analytical – Strong quantitative and analytical skills; detail-oriented and proficient in building and handling complicated data sets.
Excellent communication and presentation skills; demonstrates an ability to effectively communicate and present results that articulate key themes and messages.
Must be able to allocate time effectively and work under pressure to meet tight deadlines, handle multiple demands and competing priorities, and adapt to new ideas and change. Comfortable following direction but also contributing to the direction.
Advanced knowledge of SQL, Power Query, Excel, and Power BI is required. Familiarity with Anaplan or a similar planning tool is an asset. Experience with Tableau or Python is considered a plus.
Proactive approach to leveraging technology for process improvement and analytical enhancement. Comfortable learning and applying new tools, automation techniques, GenAI applications (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot), and advanced analytics platforms to solve complex problems, automate data analysis, rapidly prototype financial models, and deliver higher-quality insights.
Has a questioning frame of mind, asks “why” and challenges the status quo with improvements to drive change when needed.


The expected annualized base salary range for this role is $74,000-$84,000.

The actual salary offered will take into consideration a wide array of factors including, but not limited to, the individual’s skill, experience, education and training, the market compensation of the role, and the consideration to internal equity.

We value diverse experiences and perspectives. Even if your skills don’t align 100% with the listed qualifications or salary range, we encourage you to apply – you may be a great fit for this role or others in our community. Applicants may also be considered for alternative positions within the organization where their qualifications and experience align more closely with available opportunities.

We use artificial intelligence (AI) technology — alongside human review — to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. Our recruitment team remains involved in all decisions.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada as the company does not provide work permit sponsorship for this role.

Note to Recruiters: QuadReal does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to QuadReal, directly or indirectly, will be considered QuadReal property. QuadReal will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. A recruiting agency must first have a valid, written and fully executed agency agreement contract for engaged services to submit resumes.

QuadReal Property Group will provide reasonable accommodation at any time throughout the hiring process for applicants with disabilities or for those needing job postings in an alternate format. If you require accommodation, please advise the Talent Acquisition team member you are working with and include the following: Job posting #, your name and your preferred method of contact.

Title: Machine learning Engineer
Description:
Job Description

As a Machine Learning Engineer, you'll design and implement scalable, high-performance machine learning systems to support DeviantArt's vibrant online community. You'll play a key role in building innovative solutions that enhance user experiences and foster creativity within a high-traffic environment.


Develop and improve algorithms for recommendations and classification to enhance user experiences
Implement and deploy reliable machine learning systems for an active online art community
Build end-to-end systems, from data ingestion to serving results in production
Stay up-to-date with developments in data and machine learning engineering, applying them to DeviantArt systems and goals


Qualifications


5+ years of experience in Machine Learning or closely related disciplines
Understanding of machine learning algorithms, especially for recommendation and classification
Experience designing and deploying cloud-based production systems
Expertise with large-scale data processing and machine learning infrastructure
Familiarity with Python and technologies like Apache Spark, AWS, and PyTorch
Knowledge of large language models and their applications to recommendation and classification
Experience with serverless approaches or large-scale search engines like Elasticsearch or Vespa – an advantage


This is a hybrid position, and the team is expected to come to the office 1 day per week.

Additional Information

The DeviantArt Artificial Intelligence team is part of DeviantArt, the largest online social network for artists and art enthusiasts. Founded in 2000 and part of Wix since 2017, DeviantArt empowers artists to exhibit, promote, and share their works with an enthusiastic, art-centric community. With over 115 million registered users and tens of thousands of original art pieces uploaded daily, DeviantArt fosters creativity and community. The Artificial Intelligence team focuses on developing innovative solutions to enhance user experience, support artistic creativity, and ensure safe interactions within the platform.

We believe the best innovation happens when we mix deep focus work with in-person connection. While you'll work from home most of the week, we require this person to be in our Vancouver office every Thursday.

The approximate base compensation is $165,000 - 200,000 CAD In addition to base pay you will receive company RSUs as part of the compensation package.

The final offer may vary and will be determined by various factors including candidate profile and ideal qualifications.


Location: Candidates must be currently located in the Greater Vancouver Area, BC.
Work Authorization: Candidates must possess current, valid work authorization to work legally in Canada without requiring employer sponsorship now or in the future.

Title: Data Science Manager
Description:
The role and its impact

As our Data Science Manager, you will look after a small team of 3 Data Scientists within Marketing Data Science, and you will stay close to the data yourself. You will be the people manager for data scientists based in Australia, the UK and South Africa, while personally owning marketing measurement for North America, including campaign and event measurement, churn analysis and funnel effectiveness.

Your work shapes how quickly and how confidently marketing decisions get made at Xero. You will bring AI-driven insight generation and agentic analytics into everyday delivery, so the pod spends less time assembling reports and more time on the questions that move the business. You will also set the operating rhythm that helps a team spread across timezones prioritise well, share the load and keep delivery sustainable, and you will present complex analysis simply so that insight turns into decisions people act on.

The Team And How They Connect

Marketing Data Science helps Xero deliver digital, customer and marketing outcomes through insight that is increasingly AI-augmented. The wider team sits across Australia, New Zealand, the UK, South Africa and North America, so async ways of working, shared documentation and rotating meeting times are part of everyday life. You will work alongside other Data Science leads and partner closely with regional marketing teams, who rely on the pod as a thinking partner rather than a reporting service.

Initially, you will focus on


Working across SQL, Python, BigQuery, Google Analytics, Mixpanel and GTM, with dashboards and visualisation tools that people genuinely use.
Campaign and event measurement for North America, so marketing teams can see what is working and where to invest next.
Churn analysis and funnel effectiveness work that shapes acquisition, retention, engagement and personalisation.
Embedding AI-driven insight generation and agentic analytics into the pod's day to day delivery, reducing time to insight across regions.


Where And How You Can Work

This role is based in Vancouver, where our office is set up for collaboration, focus work and connection, with meeting rooms, quiet spaces and desks ready whenever you drop in. We work flexibly and take a hybrid approach, and Boost Days are our weekly in-office days with catered meals and activities that support local small businesses.

Here are some of the things we are looking for


You will bring practical marketing measurement experience across campaigns, events, churn and funnel effectiveness, and you will Go Further by turning findings into recommendations people can act on.
Working knowledge of SQL, solid Python, and a strong foundation in statistics, experimentation and causal thinking, with familiarity with Google Analytics, Mixpanel and BigQuery, form part of your everyday toolkit.
You will Go Fast by using AI-driven and agentic analytics to cut the time it takes to get from question to insight.
Coaching people you rarely share a timezone with comes naturally to you, and you will Go Together by creating rhythms that keep everyone connected and supported.
Your communication flexes easily between technical and non-technical audiences, and between local and global ones.
Comfort with ambiguity and loose direction will help you Go Bold, shaping what the team looks at next rather than waiting for the brief.


Apply even if your experience isn't a perfect match! At Xero, we hire based on your skills, passion, and the unique perspective you can bring to enhance our culture and team.

Compensation & Total Rewards

At Xero, we value the impact and skills you bring to the team. We believe in a Total Package philosophy - ensuring your value is recognized through a holistic lens that includes base salary, performance incentives, and world-class benefits.

The expected base salary range for this role is $140,000 - $190,000 CAD.

Individual pay is determined by various factors, including geography, level of experience, and the specific skills you bring to the role.

In addition to base pay, Xero’s roles are eligible for the following forms of variable compensation:


Variable Pay: Permanent employees are eligible to participate in our annual bonus and equity (RSU) programs. You may also be eligible for performance-based cash or equity (RSUs) incentives depending on your role level, and company performance.
Comprehensive Benefits: World-class health, wellness, and retirement programs. Xero Perks including Wellbeing days, generous leave, and dedicated professional development budgets.


This is a posting for an existing vacancy.

Title: Senior People Scientist, Talent Management
Description:
StackAdapt is the leading technology company that empowers marketers to reach, engage, and convert audiences with precision. With 465 billion automated optimizations per second, the AI-powered StackAdapt Marketing Platform seamlessly connects brand and performance marketing to drive measurable results across the entire customer journey. The most forward-thinking marketers choose StackAdapt to orchestrate high-impact campaigns across programmatic advertising and marketing channels.

Reporting into the Senior Talent Management Lead, we are looking for a Senior People Scientist to join our People & Culture team. In this role, you will use rigorous scientific methods to advance how StackAdapt defines, measures, and acts on talent data, and the applied skill to turn it into working tools that support better decisions across the organization. You will own critical company-wide programs, partner with senior leadership, and help us scale the people infrastructure that supports all StackAdapters.

This role partners closely with People Business Partners, People Analytics, Total Rewards, and senior leaders across all business functions. You will serve as the scientific backbone for programs that span Engineering, Revenue, and G&A — ensuring that measurement frameworks, surveys, and talent insights are rigorous, actionable, and trusted across the organization.

StackAdapt is a Remote First company although we are prioritizing candidates located in Canada for this role.

What you'll be doing:
Take end-to-end ownership to design, manage, and continuously improve company-wide talent programs including the bi-annual engagement survey, performance review cycles, and job architecture initiatives
Build measurement frameworks that assess what matters most:  performance quality, manager effectiveness, and employee engagement, using sound psychometric and statistical methods.
Build or improve internal lightweight apps, dashboards, and AI agents using low-code AI-assisted tooling to turn people data into scalable, accessible insights for leaders
Establish a working cadence with key cross-functional partners (PBPs, People Analytics, Total Rewards) and senior stakeholders to translate complex data into clear, actionable recommendations that inform overall people strategy.
Identify areas of opportunity for automation of workflows, and serve as the human-in-the-loop for AI agents. Oversee, validate, and maintain those outputs to ensure reliability, trust, and a measurable reduction in errors or manual interventions.
Navigate and manage people data and research ethics considerations to ensure we are responsibly building
What You'll Bring to the Table:
Advanced degree (MSc or PhD) in I/O Psychology, Organizational Behaviour, Social Psychology, Human Factors, Behavioural Science, or a related quantitative field — or equivalent applied depth.
Fluency in experimental design, psychometrics, survey methodology, and inferential statistics — with the ability to apply these in a fast-moving, applied setting.
Proven track record of taking ownership of active program cycles end-to-end, revisiting assumptions with data, and optimizing processes to deliver programs on time with high participation rates.
Ability to use AI and low-code tools to ship self-serve dashboards, lightweight apps, and agents that make people data accessible and drive measurable stakeholder adoption.
Strong stakeholder communication skills and demonstrated ability to build working cadences across cross-functional partners (PBPs, People Analytics, Total Rewards) to translate complex findings into clear narratives for senior leaders.
Comfort working with data and building reproducible analyses; SQL and/or Python knowledge is a strong asset, along with an aptitude for maintaining AI oversight and workflow automation.
Strong stakeholder communication skills — able to translate complex findings into clear narratives for senior leaders and cross-functional partners

Title: Advanced Data Analyst - EA Sports FC Live
Description:
Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Advanced Data Analyst - FC Live Service Forecasting

Our FC Data & Analytics team is looking for an Advanced Analyst to join our group, leading forecasting and performance modelling for FC’s live service business. Reporting to a Senior Analytics Manager, you will be part of a growing team providing data and insights around player behaviour and live content performance within the FC franchise. We’re looking for someone who combines strong quantitative forecasting expertise with business intuition, bringing the ability to translate historical trends, player behaviour, and live content strategies into actionable projections that inform decision-making. This role sits at the intersection of analytics, strategy, and live service operations - helping shape how FC plans and measures performance at scale.

What You'll Do On Our Team


Own the forecasting framework that underpins performance measurement, planning, and strategic decision-making across FC’s live service business.
Employ an extensive toolkit of financial modelling techniques, time series analysis, and a deep knowledge of their use cases.
Develop a robust model that projects our live service funnel metrics to a high degree of fidelity, incorporating player behaviour, in-game content, and macroeconomic trends.
Collaborate with partners across Product Management, Finance, and Commercial teams to align on projections, and keep the business updated on how our latest live service performance impacts our model’s assumptions.
Establish scalable forecasting processes that enable us to work with our cross-functional partners to efficiently & effectively refine our projections over time.
Lead presentations to diverse audiences including senior and executive level management, distilling complex model results into clear insights & recommendations.
Run risk and opportunity scenarios based on live content plans, new feature additions, and other potential changes in the FC product.
Mentor and collaborate with other analysts in order to collaboratively develop our forecasts, working together to drive evolutions in our modelling in this space.


What We're Looking For


A degree in a quantitative discipline (Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Finance, or similar)
7+ years of experience in a data-driven role performing quantitative analysis with big data to help guide decisions
4+ years of experience developing financial/product performance projections and forecasts using various modelling techniques
Strong experience in statistical and/or time series modelling for predictive purposes
Expertise in SQL and working with large-scale, complex datasets
Proficient in analyzing large datasets using programmatic tools (e.g. Python, R)
Experience with data visualization software (e.g. Tableau, PowerBI)
Strong capabilities in project management processes
Very comfortable presenting analysis in an executive facing environment

Title: AI/ML Engineer
Description:
Applied AI/ML Scientist - Interviews are onsite in Vancouver

Location: Onsite

Salary: $110K – $120K




Location: This is onsite 5 days a week in downtown Vancouver.




Note: Candidates need experience in the biomedical domain, and at least 6 years of work experience




About the Role

We’re looking for an Applied AI/ML Scientist to help design, validate, and operationalize Mimik’s health agents. This role sits at the intersection of research and product engineering, with a strong focus on experimentation, multimodal modeling, personalization, evaluation, and real-world deployment. You will work on models that turn physiological and behavioral data into safe, structured outputs that power Mimik’s member experience.

Key Responsibilities

Model Design: Design and evaluate models for Mimik’s on-device health agents across wearable, CGM, EHR, lab, and behavioral data.
Translation: Translate emerging research into practical implementations for personalized health inference under mobile and edge constraints.
Architecture: Define feature pipelines, training data strategy, personalization logic, and structured output schemas for agent outputs.
Evaluation: Build experiments and evaluation frameworks for accuracy, safety, calibration, and member-level usefulness.
Engineering Collaboration: Work closely with product and engineering to move promising models into production mobile workflows, including on-device inference and privacy-preserving deployment.
Domain Focus: Contribute to model and dataset selection for key domains such as sleep, stress, and metabolic health.

Requirements

Experience: Strong applied ML / data science experience in time-series, multimodal, or physiological data.
Frameworks: Experience designing experiments, evaluation frameworks, and model quality metrics.
Technology: Experience with agentic LLM systems.
Mindset: Ability to work across research and engineering, not just modeling in isolation.

Nice to Have

Experience with on-device / edge ML, quantization, or mobile deployment.
Familiarity with wearable, CGM, EHR, or lab data.
Experience integrating model outputs into product systems built on JavaScript / TypeScript platforms.

Title: Applied Scientist II, Alexa Daily Essentials Science and Analytics
Description:
Description

On the Alexa Daily Essentials Science and Analytics team, we build intelligence systems that power AI-driven experiences for customer-facing features used by hundreds of millions of people daily. Our team applies foundation models in novel ways — designing agentic systems that reason, plan, and act autonomously over complex data, and rigorously evaluating their performance so that every architecture decision is grounded in measured quality. We're not actively training foundation models. We're pushing the frontier of how they're applied — through agentic architectures, reinforcement learning, retrieval-augmented generation, and evaluation science.

As an Applied Scientist II, you will design agentic AI systems that autonomously detect, diagnose, and act on signals across Alexa's product surface. You'll build the evaluation science that validates these systems, prototype novel AI-powered features that create new value for customers, and apply reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior through outcome signals. You'll own science end-to-end — from rapid prototyping through production deployment — working directly with engineers and product leaders to ship systems that impact how millions of customers interact with Alexa daily. This is a role for a scientist who brings rigor to evaluation, creativity to invention, and pragmatism to delivery.

Key job responsibilities


Design and implement agentic AI systems — multi-step reasoning, tool use, planning, and orchestration — that autonomously surface intelligence and take action over complex, evolving data
Apply reinforcement learning techniques to improve agent routing, decision-making, and task resolution quality from outcome signals
Build evaluation and benchmarking frameworks — automated test suites, LLM-as-judge pipelines, competitive benchmarks, and regression detection across model versions and prompt strategies
Prototype and develop novel AI-powered features — information extraction, proactive recommendations, multi-agent collaboration — from concept through production launch
Build RAG pipelines and knowledge retrieval systems that ground agent reasoning in trusted data
Design and execute experiments end-to-end — hypothesis generation, causal analysis, and results interpretation that directly shape product roadmaps
Communicate findings to technical and non-technical audiences — influencing architecture decisions, model selection, and product strategy through rigorous evaluation


A day in the life

You might start by analyzing reward signal distributions from your latest RL experiment on agent routing — identifying where the policy improved and where exploration is still needed. Mid-morning, you prototype a new cross-feature experience, testing whether extraction models can reliably surface actionable items from customer content. After lunch, you run your eval suite against a new model version — comparing benchmark scores across reasoning depth, tool-use reliability, and output consistency to inform an architecture decision. Later, you pair with an engineer to add a new capability to an agent's tool registry, then validate it doesn't degrade downstream quality. You end the day designing an A/B test for a proactive feature your team is launching.

About The Team

We're a small, high-ownership team building agentic intelligence systems for Alexa — one of the world's most widely used AI products, reaching hundreds of millions of customers across devices, languages, and contexts. We apply foundation models in novel ways: systems that reason over temporal data, learn from outcomes through reinforcement, autonomously detect regressions, and surface insights that previously required weeks of manual analysis. Our scientists prototype new features, benchmark rigorously, and ship from research through production. If you want to build at the frontier of applied AI — agentic systems, reinforcement learning, evaluation science — with real users and real impact at Alexa scale, this is the team.

Basic Qualifications


3+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience
PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience
Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
Experience with one of the following areas: machine learning technologies, Reinforcement Learning, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing (NLP) or related applications


Preferred Qualifications


Experience in professional software development
Experience creating novel algorithms and advancing the state of the art
Experience designing or working with agentic AI systems (tool-use, multi-step reasoning, RAG, multi-agent orchestration)
Experience building automated evaluation frameworks or LLM-as-judge systems

Description & Requirements

Job Title: Gameplay Data Science Engineer

Location: Hybrid - Vancouver or Los Angeles

Reports to: Technical Director

Job Summary

Founded in 2010, Respawn was created with the philosophy that when talented people have creative freedom, they’ll make extraordinary games that achieve the unexpected. Respawn Entertainment is the Academy Award-winning studio behind Apex Legends, Titanfall, and Star Wars Jedi titles. Join us to help shape the future of one of the world’s leading live service franchises: Apex Legends.

As a Gameplay & Data Science Engineer, you will drive the Research & Development of advanced bot behaviors and AI frameworks to enhance the Apex Legends experience. You will work at the intersection of data science and gameplay programming, utilizing machine learning and reinforcement learning to create intelligent agents. Working closely with gameplay teams, game designers, and producers, you will implement robust AI systems that improve game quality and player engagement. Your work will ensure our AI is of outstanding quality and provides the best experience for our players.

Responsibilities


Lead R&D efforts for game bots using machine learning, reinforcement learning, and neural networks to create realistic agent behaviors.
Design, implement, and maintain gameplay-focused AI frameworks, including Utility AI systems, directly within the game engine.
Collaborate with gameplay teams and designers to translate creative vision into technical specifications and scalable AI solutions.
Develop and program algorithms to structure and analyze gameplay data to improve bot performance and decision-making.
Optimize AI systems and data pipelines to ensure high performance and stability across consoles and dedicated servers.


Required Qualifications


5+ years of experience in data science, machine learning engineering, or gameplay programming within the games industry.
Strong proficiency in C/C++ and Python for both engine-level implementation and algorithmic development.
Hands-on experience with reinforcement learning, supervised/unsupervised learning, and AI architectures like Utility AI.
Experience with large-scale computing frameworks, big-data techniques, and building scalable data pipelines.
Solid foundation in mathematics, statistics, and optimization theory applied to game AI and machine learning.
Bachelor's or advanced degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.


Pay Transparency - North America

Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at EA.
